claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning an eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**First, can you tell me: What is the age of the child (or children) you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Specifically, please let me know:
- How old is/are the child(ren)?
- Are they under 16, between 16-19, or 20 or over?

If you have multiple children, please list each one with their age so I can assess each one.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 4 years old. He lives at home with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! That's really helpful. So you have **Alex, who is 4 years old** and lives with you in the UK.

Since Alex is under 16, let me continue with the eligibility check. The next step is to verify that Alex is not working full-time, which is required for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

(For a 4-year-old, the answer will almost certainly be no paid work, but I need to confirm this for the eligibility check.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's only 4! He just goes to nursery during the day.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Alex is just 4 years old and at nursery, so definitely not in paid work. Let me continue with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit?**

(Again, for a 4-year-old, this should be no, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's just 4, so that wouldn't apply to him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great, that's confirmed. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

(For a 4-year-old, this won't apply, but I need to confirm for completeness.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's only 4 years old!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! Alex is just 4 years old and at nursery, so he's definitely not in an apprenticeship. Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status to ensure you meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

**Can you tell me about your residency situation?**

Here are the main paths that would qualify you:

1. **Normally live in the UK** - You live in the UK most of the time
2. **Settled status under EU Settlement Scheme** - You have settled status
3. **Pre-settled status and working** - You have pre-settled status and are earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 months
4. **Pre-settled status and actively seeking work** - You have pre-settled status and looking for work (can claim as jobseeker for up to 91 days)
5. **Pre-settled status with sufficient resources** - You have pre-settled status, sufficient financial resources, and not claiming certain benefits
6. **Pre-settled status and studying** - You have pre-settled status, studying with sufficient resources
7. **Pre-settled status as family member** - You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national
8. **Crown servant living abroad** - You're a Crown servant living abroad in qualifying circumstances

Which of these applies to your situation? Or are you normally resident in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I mentioned earlier that Alex and I live here.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for confirming that. You normally live in the UK, which satisfies the residency requirement. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Are you responsible for Alex?**

Responsibility means either:
1. **Living with the child** - You live with Alex (which you mentioned you do)
2. **Contributing to the child's upkeep** - You pay at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care (food, clothes, housing, etc.)
3. **Paying maintenance** - You make maintenance payments under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned Alex lives at home with you, it sounds like you live together. Can you confirm that you are responsible for Alex's care and upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely - Alex lives at home with me and I look after him completely. I provide everything for him - food, clothes, housing, all his care.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You clearly have responsibility for Alex and are meeting all his needs. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied for it?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent (if applicable) also claiming or planning to claim?
- Is anyone else claiming Alex as a dependent?

I need to confirm whether you're the only person claiming for Alex, or if there might be another claimant involved.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm the only one claiming for him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Where does Alex currently live and what is his situation?**

- Does Alex live with you at home normally?
- Or is he in hospital, in care, or fostered?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives with me at home, though he was in care for a short time recently - just a couple of months. But he's back home with me now.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Since Alex is currently living with you at home normally now, let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you personally paying for Alex's housing and care, or is the council contributing towards these costs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. I'm paying for everything myself - his housing, food, everything he needs.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's all the information I need. You have met all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me confirm your eligibility:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me record your final eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **Good News! You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit**

**For: Alex (age 4)**

---

### **Why You're Eligible:**

Alex meets all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit:

1. ✅ **Age**: Alex is 4 years old (under 16)
2. ✅ **Not working full-time**: Alex is at nursery and not in paid work
3. ✅ **No disqualifying benefits**: Alex is not receiving ESA or Universal Credit in his own name
4. ✅ **Not an apprentice**: Not applicable at age 4
5. ✅ **UK Residency**: You normally live in the UK
6. ✅ **Responsible for Alex**: You live with Alex and provide for all his needs
7. ✅ **Only claimant**: You are the sole claimant for Alex
8. ✅ **Normal living situation**: Alex lives at home with you
9. ✅ **Council not paying**: You are paying for all of Alex's accommodation and maintenance

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate**
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay some or all of the benefit back through tax
5. **Payment frequency** - You'll typically receive payments every 4 weeks

For more information and to apply, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Congratulations on your eligibility! If you have any other questions, feel free to ask.

Alex meets all eligibility requirements for Child Benefit.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex. As a 4-year-old child living with you in the UK under your care and responsibility, with no other claimants and no council contributions, Alex qualifies for Child Benefit under all the required criteria."]
